record.field: Describe a model's readable fields (label, type, help, selection options and relation target) so their values can be interpreted. Returns "fields" (readable) and "hidden" (fields forbidden to AI).

Search and read records of a model. Accepts an optional Odoo domain such as [["is_company", "=", true]], an explicit field list, a limit (200 at most, and by default), an offset and an order. Without a field list, the stored fields are returned; ask for computed ones explicitly. "has_more" tells whether more records match: read the next page with the offset increased by the limit, keeping the same domain and order; "total_count" tells how many records match in all, so do not page through records to count them. Relational fields are returned as record IDs; read the related model to get the details of those records. Dates and times are in UTC. A requested field missing from the records is not available (forbidden to AI, binary, or not readable for the current user), so do not retry it; get_fields lists the readable fields, and the forbidden ones under "hidden". A field whose value cannot be computed for the current user is left out and listed in "inaccessible_fields"; do not retry it either.
Count the records of a model matching an optional Odoo domain, such as [["is_company", "=", true]], without reading them. Use it for "how many" questions instead of paging through search_read.

Group the records of a model matching an optional Odoo domain and compute totals per group, in the database. Use it for totals, averages, counts per category and distributions over time instead of reading and adding up records. "groupby" lists field names; a date field takes a granularity: "date_order:month" (day, week, month, quarter, year). "aggregates" lists "field:function" specs, with function one of count, count_distinct, sum, avg, min, max, bool_and, bool_or, and "__count" for the number of records (the default). Without "groupby", one group sums up all matching records. Each group is an object keyed by those specs; relational values are record IDs, so read the related model for their names. "order" sorts the groups by a spec, such as "amount_total:sum desc". At most 500 groups are returned (100 by default); "has_more" tells whether more exist: read them with the offset increased by the limit. Only fields listed by get_fields, and stored, can be grouped or aggregated.
